text:
# Short answer

For a typical full-size fridge, get a pure sine wave power station with **at least 1,300 W of surge** and about **1,000-1,500 Wh for roughly a day**. If you want 1.5-2 days, or room for other loads, look at **~2,000 Wh**.

## Why those numbers

Three checks matter:

1. **Running watts:** A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station covers ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Startup surge:** The compressor spikes briefly when it starts. Estimates range from about 1,000-1,200 W for a typical fridge up to 2,400 W for large or older units ([BlackBox](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). Surge is the spec that most often makes a station fail, so check it first. Also look for a pure sine wave inverter.
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time. One guide uses a 41 W daily average for an ENERGY STAR 18 cu ft fridge, which is about 1,400 Wh per day once you allow for inverter losses and headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

For your own fridge, take the kWh/year on its yellow EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average twice the ENERGY STAR figure.

## Rough runtimes (HomeGridHQ's estimates)

| Capacity | Approx. runtime |
|---|---|
| ~1,000 Wh | ~17 hours |
| ~1,500 Wh | ~25 hours |
| ~2,000 Wh | ~33 hours |
| ~3,000 Wh | ~2 days |

Opening the door less, a warm kitchen, and other devices on the same station will change these numbers. Plan for a margin.

## Options from these sources

- **~2,000 Wh, longest runtime:** [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous output, and expands up to 8 kWh. It's listed at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the listing says was tested in BLUETTI's cart. That link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Checkout shows the final price. Details are on the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l).
- **~2,000 Wh alternative:** [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W AC output, 3,000 W peak, and pure sine wave. It was $699.99 after coupon on Anker's page.
- **~1,000-1,500 Wh, about a day:** BlackBox picks the BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W with 2,700 W peak, roughly $399-699) and the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (roughly $449-799). I don't have direct buy links for these. Prices and links are in the [BlackBox guide](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage).

## Caveats

- Skip small, device-oriented units such as ~300 Wh models. They often fall below the surge requirement or last only a few hours.
- Prices in these results change often and some come from affiliate sites, so confirm at checkout.
- If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year, and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
